C1.rule: Mechanical, one owned file, fully specified, no design choice

C2.rule: Bounded implementation or tests, clear spec, one or two owned files and their tests

C3.rule: Cross-module design; changes a gate or the ledger contract; wrong means every project inherits it

C4.rule: Planning, merging, reconciling, anything in a project's real data, a sponsor decision

phases.name: Traceability
phases.goal: Keep user-facing guide claims, architecture boundaries, implementation, and verification visibly connected.
phases.exit: Every traceability row names its requirement, guide and architecture sections, implementation files, verification command, receipt or refusal, owner, and status.

items.title: Track guide-to-architecture evidence as a first-class map
items.what: Carry Loom-style traceability rows in the proposal ledger and render them in the project tracker so a guide claim can be followed through architecture, implementation, verification, and its receipt or refusal.
items.done: The ledger validates the complete traceability chain; the generated tracker renders it as a table; focused tests and tracker validation pass.

traceability.receipt_or_refusal: receipt: focused tracker suite green; refusal: incomplete rows fail ledger validation
